payload.executive_summary: Candidate B01B implements the Implementation Council as a sequential staged pipeline (O1) with a big-bang milestone strategy and high HITL strictness. The architecture maximizes determinism, auditability, and traceability by executing one stage at a time through a linear state machine (Intake → WorkPlanning → Generate → PatchApply → Validate → Review → Patch → Judge → Freeze). All artifacts are produced, validated, and checkpointed at each stage boundary before advancing. A single comprehensive freeze event gates the entire Implementation Freeze Bundle against all closure validators. High HITL involvement is applied at every escalation point—ChangeRequests, protected-path modifications, secrets detection, gate waivers, and retry-budget exhaustion—to mitigate risks of scope expansion (K1), audit spine breakage (K2), and policy bypass (K5). The big-bang milestone strategy means all deliverables are reviewed holistically before any part is considered done, preventing incremental drift. This is the most conservative and risk-averse candidate, trading wall-clock speed for maximum predictability and governance rigor.

architecture_choice.rationale: O1 is selected because the branch mandate (B01) requires maximum conservatism, determinism, and auditability. The sequential staged pipeline provides the simplest reproducible execution model with unambiguous stage boundaries, a linear audit trail, and straightforward checkpoint/resume semantics. It directly satisfies CNS1 (separation of powers via orchestrator-owned linear state machine), CNS3 (durable audit spine with clear stage checkpoints), CNS6 (single evidence standard enforced at each gate), and CNS8 (workspace governance with deterministic context packs compiled per stage). The lack of parallelism eliminates merge-conflict risks (K12) entirely and simplifies workspace partitioning. High HITL strictness compensates for the single-lane bottleneck by ensuring manual scrutiny at every escalation point, which aligns with the extremely risk-averse posture. O2 was rejected because parallel lanes introduce merge/integration complexity incompatible with the conservative posture. O3 was rejected because partial-freeze semantics add downstream consumer complexity unnecessary for a big-bang strategy. O4 was rejected because the monolithic boundary weakens internal auditability and role separation enforcement.
architecture_choice.high_level_dataflow: plan_package_final.json + repo_context.json + workspace_context.json → [C3 Intake Gate: schema validation, run_manifest + event_log init, stage_handoff] → [C4 Work Plan Compiler: decompose R#/AT#/O#/K# into ordered tasks, emit work_plan.json] → [C5 Writer Pod: consume context pack per task batch, emit diff-only patchset JSON] → [C1 Orchestrator: apply patchsets via PatchApply with forbidden-path/op-cap enforcement] → [C6 Validator Engine: run build/test/lint/typecheck/security/secrets scans, emit test_results.json + quality_reports.json] → [C7 Reviewer Pod: read-only review, emit review_findings.json with RFC 6901 pointers] → [C8 Patcher Pod: if repairs needed, emit RFC 6902 patches / replacement patchsets within bounded loops] → [C9 Judge Pod: evaluate all outputs, emit trace_report.json + freeze recommendation] → [C10 Freeze Assembler: collect and validate full Implementation Freeze Bundle, run final integrity/reproducibility/workspace-integrity checks, emit decision_record.json + release_bundle.json]. C2 Workspace Gateway mediates all artifact/workspace IO throughout. C1 Orchestrator owns routing, budgets, tool permissions, checkpoint/stage_handoff enforcement, and HITL triggers at every boundary.
key_design_decisions: Sequential execution only: one active stage at a time eliminates parallel merge conflicts and simplifies checkpoint/resume to a single linear chain of stage_handoffs.
Big-bang freeze: no partial freezes; the entire Implementation Freeze Bundle is assembled and gated in one event, ensuring holistic review.
High HITL strictness: every ChangeRequest, protected-path modification, secrets detection, gate waiver, retry-budget exhaustion, and permission expansion triggers mandatory human approval.
Deterministic context packs compiled by orchestrator at each stage boundary from workspace_index with explicit selection rules and byte/token bounds.
Workspace Gateway (C2) is the sole API for all artifact and workspace IO, enforcing canonical/non-canonical separation, versioning, secrets blocking, and checkpoint/restore.
Writer/Reviewer/Judge separation enforced by orchestrator output-type allowlists and multi-vendor routing constraints per stage.
Smallest-passing-repair selection: fewest operations → fewest bytes → first-generated, enforced deterministically by orchestrator.
All repairs via RFC 6902 JSON Patch (JSON artifacts) or diff-only replacement patchsets (code), with orchestrator-enforced op caps and forbidden-path rules.
Secrets scanning mandatory at every checkpoint and pre-freeze; any detection blocks persistence and triggers HITL.

decision_log.question: Which architecture option should be selected for the Implementation Council?
decision_log.choice: O1 — Sequential staged pipeline with explicit council role pods
decision_log.rationale: The branch mandate (B01) requires maximum conservatism, determinism, and auditability. O1 provides the simplest reproducible execution model with unambiguous stage boundaries, a linear audit trail, and straightforward checkpoint/resume. It eliminates merge-conflict risks (K12) entirely and directly satisfies CNS1, CNS3, CNS6, CNS8. High HITL strictness compensates for single-lane throughput limitations.
alternatives_considered: O2 — Task-parallel fan-out/fan-in: rejected due to merge/integration complexity incompatible with conservative posture and high HITL overhead for conflict resolution
O3 — Checkpoint-driven micro-cycle with partial freeze: rejected because partial-freeze semantics add downstream consumer complexity unnecessary for big-bang strategy
O4 — Monolithic Implementation Council: rejected because internal opacity weakens auditability and role separation enforcement
what_would_change_this_decision: Requirement for significantly faster wall-clock execution on repos with many independent tasks
Evidence that sequential execution consistently exceeds token/time budgets for target repositories
Reduction in HITL strictness requirement allowing automated conflict resolution

evidence_pointers.quote: Simplest reproducible execution model: one active stage and a linear audit trail.

evidence_pointers.note: Branch B01 mandate for O1 with big-bang and high HITL

decision_log.question: What milestone strategy should be used?
decision_log.choice: Big-bang: single comprehensive freeze event at the end of the linear pipeline
decision_log.rationale: The branch mandate specifies big-bang milestone style. All deliverables are reviewed holistically before any part is considered done, preventing incremental drift and ensuring all acceptance tests and closure gates are satisfied in one comprehensive pass. This aligns with the extremely risk-averse posture.
alternatives_considered: Incremental milestones with partial freezes (O3-style): rejected per branch mandate
Parallel milestone tracks: rejected as incompatible with sequential O1 architecture
what_would_change_this_decision: Evidence that holistic review is infeasible due to bundle size or review capacity
Requirement for incremental delivery to downstream consumers before full completion

evidence_pointers.note: Big-bang milestone strategy specified by branch
evidence_pointers.quote: The entire implementation plan is executed as a single, sequential pipeline, culminating in one final freeze event.

decision_log.question: How should HITL strictness be configured?
decision_log.choice: High HITL strictness: mandatory human approval at every escalation point defined in hitl_policy
decision_log.rationale: The branch risk posture is extremely risk-averse, prioritizing auditability and predictability. High HITL involvement directly mitigates K1 (scope expansion), K2 (audit spine breakage), K4 (security vulnerabilities), K5 (policy bypass), and K7 (secrets leakage) through manual scrutiny at every trigger point.
alternatives_considered: Medium HITL: automated handling for lower-severity escalations — rejected per branch mandate
Low HITL: minimal human involvement — rejected as incompatible with risk-averse posture
what_would_change_this_decision: Demonstrated reliability of automated validators sufficient to reduce manual review burden
Organizational decision to accept higher automation risk for faster throughput

evidence_pointers.note: Full list of HITL trigger conditions
High HITL strictness and sandboxed tooling

decision_log.question: How should tool permissions be enforced?
decision_log.choice: Sandboxed tooling with deny-by-default per-stage permission matrix as defined in risk_gov tool_policy
decision_log.rationale: Sandboxed tooling level is specified by the branch governance posture. Deny-by-default with explicit per-stage allowlists ensures that no tool capability is available unless explicitly permitted, directly mitigating K5 (repo protection bypass), K7 (secrets leakage), K15 (supply-chain risk), and K19 (misconfigured permissions). Network is denied by default across all stages.
alternatives_considered: Permissive tooling with post-hoc audit: rejected as incompatible with risk-averse posture and CNS1/CNS9
Partially sandboxed with broader defaults: rejected per branch governance posture
what_would_change_this_decision: Target repositories requiring network access during build/test that cannot use offline mirrors
Evidence that sandbox overhead causes unacceptable performance degradation

decision_log.question: How should the acceptance strategy work for this candidate?
decision_log.choice: Single comprehensive freeze bundle passing all gates at end of linear pipeline; all R# requirements and AT# acceptance tests satisfied in one go
decision_log.rationale: Aligned with big-bang milestone strategy. A single freeze event ensures holistic validation and prevents partial or premature release. All 23 acceptance tests (AT1–AT23) must pass, and all closure gates (build/test/lint/typecheck, integrity, workspace integrity, risk closure, reproducibility, trace completeness) must be satisfied before freeze is permitted.
alternatives_considered: Incremental acceptance with partial freeze bundles: rejected per branch mandate
Staged acceptance with intermediate sign-offs: rejected as adding complexity without benefit under big-bang strategy
what_would_change_this_decision: Evidence that single-pass validation is infeasible for the target scope

evidence_pointers.quote: Freeze SHALL be permitted only when all deterministic, code-owned closure gates pass

supplemental_evaluations.title: Risk Coverage Assessment for O1 Sequential Pipeline
supplemental_evaluations.notes: O1 eliminates K12 (merge/integration conflicts) entirely since there is no parallel execution. K1 (scope expansion) is mitigated by sequential review at every stage plus high HITL. K2 (audit spine) benefits from simple linear checkpoint chain. K6 (flaky tests) risk is concentrated since a single lane stall blocks all progress — mitigated by deterministic retry/quarantine/escalation policy. K9 (context pack overflow) is a concern since artifacts accumulate linearly across stages — mitigated by bounded context pack selection rules and aggressive filtering. K16 (over-broad refactors) is addressed by patchset size caps enforced at PatchApply stage. The primary residual risk is long-horizon token/time budget exhaustion due to serialized execution, which is accepted under the conservative posture with HITL escalation as the fallback.

evidence.note: O1 identified risks: token/time budgets, context accumulation, flaky stalls

supplemental_evaluations.title: Open Questions Impact on This Candidate
supplemental_evaluations.notes: Several blocking open questions (Q1–Q15) affect implementation details but do not invalidate the architecture choice. Q1 (target ecosystems) determines validator entrypoints in repo_context.json. Q2 (workspace backend) determines C2 implementation. Q7 (diff format) determines patchset artifact internals. Q8 (smallest-passing-repair) is resolved by DEC specification (fewest ops → fewest bytes → first-generated) but may need refinement. Q9 (conflict resolution) is N/A for O1 since there is no parallelism. Q13 (incremental implementation under budget pressure) is the most significant: under big-bang strategy, budget exhaustion without partial freeze means the run fails and must be restarted or escalated via HITL. This is an accepted trade-off under the conservative posture.

synthesis_warnings.summary: Big-bang strategy with no partial-freeze capability means token/time budget exhaustion results in total run failure requiring restart. Q13 (incremental implementation under budget pressure) is blocking and unresolved. If target repositories are large, this candidate may be infeasible without a budget-exhaustion mitigation plan.
